newsitem.title: USA: Fortress says Lazard unit to invest $75mln.
newsitem.headline: Fortress says Lazard unit to invest $75mln.

text.p: Fortress Group said Friday a Lazard Freres Real Estate Investors LLC affiliate agreed to invest $75 million in the company for a 36.4 percent stake.
The home maufacturer said the deal gives Lazard affiliate Prometheus Homebuilders LLC a 36.4 percent stake, or 6.73 million shares, of the company.

Fortress said its board of directors, management and certain insiders, who collectively control about 63 percent of the company, have approved the transaction. The company added it expects to close the deal in December.

The deal calls for Prometheus to buy about $35 million of Fortress newly-issued class AA convertible preferred stock, which is convertible at $6 a share and pays a six percent annual dividend, the company said.

Fortress said it can require conversion when the average closing price of its common stock for the 90 days preceding conversion equals or exceeds $12. The conversion price can decrease if its common stock trades at less than $12.01 after four years, Fortress added.

Fortress said Prometheus also will invest $40 million in newly-issued class AB convertible redeemable preferred stock, which will pay a 12 percent preferred dividend and is convertible in the fourth year at a price equal to 95 percent of Fortress share price.

Prometheus also will receive one million warrants exerciseable at $7 a share. The number of warrants may increase if Fortress shares trade at less than $20.01 after four years, the company said, adding the warrants' exercise price could decrease if its shares trade at less than $12.01 after four years.
The warrants have a seven-year term and are exerciseable in the second year of the deal, Fortress added.
Fortress said it expected to close the first part of the deal in September when Prometheus will buy $12 million to 15 million of the class AB stock.
The company said Prometheus will also buy about 900,000 shares from the company's original founders for $5.50 a share, or about $4.9 million.
Prometheus also will consider investing up to an additional $25 million in 1999, Fortress said.
